# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

## THE READER (who consumes what you edit)
At runtime these capabilities are read by `rits/Qwen/Qwen3-8B` — capability tier: **strong**. The reader is a capable general model, but less robust than frontier on long or ambiguous context. Keep instructions clear and reasonably explicit; add a worked example for tricky formats; prefer code enforcement for behavioral rules over trusting inference.
Optimize your edits for THIS reader's capability level, not for your own. When the reader is weaker than you, prefer explicit rules, worked examples, and code enforcement over terse prose you would personally infer.


Focus: every failing task on the val split. Current val reward 0.244: 1 solid / 2 flaky / 7 failing of 10 tasks.



GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `## What you are editing (the allowed edit space)
The capability under optimization is composed of these editable artifact(s). Use the FULL edit space below — do not limit yourself to trivial wording tweaks.
- **system-prompt** — Optimize an agent's system prompt / policy text (instructions, output contract, decision policy).
  - Allowed edits: Edit the prompt/policy text: instructions, decision policy, and the output contract. Prefer sharpening rules the traces show the agent breaking; do not just append more preamble.
  - Full guidance (read it): ./guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.

## The THREE TESTS every change must pass (this is the whole game)
Before you keep any edit, confirm all three. Drop any edit that fails even one.
1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`
   (reward 0, partial-credit, or communication/omission). Never edit for a hypothetical
   problem, and never edit on account of a task whose failure is an environment fault.
2. **SAFE (bounded blast radius)** — the real regression question is *behavioral*:
   **would this edit change what the agent DOES on ANY currently-passing task?** Two
   blast-radius classes:
   - **BOUNDED** — an ADDITIVE rule that applies only under a stated condition present in
     the failing cases, or a clarification of an output contract the passing tasks already
     satisfy. This is the SAFE default — prefer it.
   - **UNBOUNDED** — any edit to a GLOBAL decision/permission/refusal rule, or a rewrite /
     reordering / deletion that changes the instruction the agent follows on every task. It
     changes behavior across the ENTIRE class, including tasks where the original behavior
     was the gold answer. Allowed ONLY if the new behavior is correct for EVERY task in
     that class AND you have read the currently-passing tasks in the class and confirmed
     none relied on the old wording.
   Name the passing tasks in each edit's blast-radius class and state which class it is.
   A regression wastes the whole candidate (the gate rejects a net-zero), not one task.
3. **VERIFIED** — you have shown it actually fixes its target (see VERIFY-THE-FIX). An
   edit you cannot verify is a guess — drop it.

Quality AND breadth: ship every fix that passes the three tests — the more clusters you
cover safely, the bigger the gain. The only edits to leave out are the speculative ones
(an edit that fails a test), not real fixes you ran out of patience for. Don't re-add
anything `LEDGER.md` / `JOURNAL.md` show was already tried and rejected.

  missing-rule, worked example, ordered procedure, consolidation of conflicting text). Do
  not invent change types from memory — take them from the skill, and deliberately apply
  MULTIPLE DIFFERENT types this iteration, matching each cluster to the strongest type the

- `./guidance/diagnose/SKILL.md` — the failure-clustering method. Use it.

  the actual traces for the clusters you'll fix, don't rely on the summary alone.
- `./LEDGER.md` — FACTS (read-only): every prior iteration's outcome + the exact tasks it

- `./JOURNAL.md` — the accumulating handover. Each entry is the optimizer's INTENT, and

## Process (do this, then STOP)
**Parallelism:** Your agent supports parallel subagents/worktrees (see ./guidance/optimizer/claude-code.md). FAN OUT to cover MANY clusters at once: one read-only subagent per trajectory-group to diagnose, then one edit-subagent per issue (each in its own worktree), then MERGE every edit into this ONE candidate with no conflicts. This is how a single iteration fixes many issues across many trajectories, not just the biggest one.
1. Read your capability SKILL(s) + the diagnose method + the cross-iteration files
   (LEDGER facts, JOURNAL handover, RUNMAP for clusters you'll touch).
2. Diagnose THIS iteration's `./trajectories/` ONLY (not stale signatures). Cluster ALL
   failures by shared root cause — total, partial-credit, AND communication/omission.
   **First separate ENVIRONMENT faults from capability failures** (see above): a cluster
   whose every trace dies on the same infrastructure error is not yours to fix.
   RANK the remaining clusters by LEVERAGE = (# failing tasks × trials × score
   recoverable), biggest first — but plan to fix ALL of them this iteration.
3. For EACH cluster, pick the strongest improvement TYPE from the capability SKILL(s)
   (cross-check the FAILURE TYPE section next) and draft the edit. Across the iteration
   use MULTIPLE different types from the skills, not the same one repeatedly. Run each
   edit through the THREE TESTS; keep it only if it passes all three.
4. Ship every passing edit together in this ONE candidate — cover as many clusters as you
   can SAFELY (that is the win), and never include an edit that fails a test.
5. Fill `PROCESS.md` and APPEND your entry to `JOURNAL.md`. STOP.

## Choose the lever by FAILURE TYPE
Pick the strongest lever your capability's edit space offers (see `./guidance/<cap>/`).
Every lever below is a PROSE edit — the point is that they are not all the same edit.

- **OUTPUT-CONTRACT / FORMAT MISS** — the work is right but the graded artifact is wrong
  (written to the wrong place, wrong shape, wrong precision, formula instead of value,
  extra cells/keys touched). **Default strong lever: state the contract exactly, once, in
  imperative form, at the point of use** — the precise path/shape/type, what must NOT be
  touched, and the one-line check the agent can run before finishing. This is the
  highest-yield, lowest-regression prompt edit; reach for it first.
- **SKIPPED / OUT-OF-ORDER STEP (behavioral)** — the agent knows the rule and skips it, or
  acts before verifying. Do NOT restate the rule. **Make it structurally unavoidable:** an
  ORDERED, numbered procedure with the step as a precondition of the next one, or a
  short pre-finish checklist the agent must satisfy — phrased as work to perform, not as
  advice to remember.
- **CAPABILITY GAP / ACTION STALL** — the agent has no reliable way to do the thing, or it
  narrates a multi-step action then never executes it. Prose CANNOT invent a missing
  capability: what it can do is supply the concrete METHOD — a worked, copyable procedure
  (the exact sequence, API/idiom, and end-to-end example) that the agent can execute
  directly. If no wording could make the task achievable, say so in PROCESS.md rather than
  shipping a hopeful paragraph; a hard zero does not move on emphasis.
- **KNOWLEDGE GAP** — a format/criterion/fact the agent genuinely cannot derive → state it
  precisely, and only it. Don't restate a rule the agent already has; that's a skipped
  step (use structure), not a knowledge gap.
- **DECISION / PERMISSION (ACT vs REFUSE)** — the agent made the wrong call on a decision
  the prompt governs. **This is the most dangerous cluster to fix wrong.** NEVER loosen,
  broaden, or alter a GLOBAL decision/permission/refusal rule — a global change (e.g.
  "restricted records MAY now be modified") flips behavior for the WHOLE class and
  regresses every currently-passing task where the stricter behavior was the gold answer
  (this exact mistake sank a prior run). Instead add an ADDITIVE rule that NARROWS: state
  the exact discriminating CONDITION that separates the qualifying cases, so only those
  change.
- **CONFLICT / BLOAT** — two instructions disagree, or the rule that matters is buried in
  prose the agent skims. CONSOLIDATE: resolve the contradiction and hoist the decisive
  rule to where it is read. Deleting is allowed here — but only text you have shown to be
  redundant or contradicted, never a rule a passing task depends on.

Also fix **recovery guidance** — what the agent should do when its own attempt errors —
when a recoverable error stranded it mid-task. High leverage, low risk.

## VERIFY-THE-FIX (do this for EACH kept edit — it satisfies the VERIFIED + SAFE tests)
A prompt edit cannot be unit-tested, so verify it against the TRACES, concretely:
- **Point at the evidence:** quote the line(s) from the failing trace that the edit
  addresses, and state what the agent would have done differently had the edit been
  present. "It would have been clearer" is not verification.
- **Contract / format edit:** confirm the value you now state matches what the SCORER
  compares (read the answer/expected artifact in the trace or the benchmark source) — not
  merely what the old prompt said. A confidently-stated wrong contract is worse than none.
- **Structural edit (ordered procedure / checklist):** confirm the skipped step is now a
  precondition of a step the agent must take, not just mentioned earlier.
- **Decision / permission edit:** the SAFE check is BEHAVIORAL. Enumerate the
  currently-passing tasks in the SAME decision class and confirm the edit would NOT flip
  the agent's action on any of them — in particular that it does not make the agent newly
  ACT where a passing task's gold answer was to refuse. If you cannot enumerate and check
  that class, the edit is UNBOUNDED and unverified — rescope it to the qualifying cases.
- **Deletion / consolidation:** name the tasks whose traces show the removed text was
  unused or contradicted, and confirm no passing trace relies on it.

Record one line per edit in PROCESS.md, e.g.
`trace <task>: wrote formula not value → contract line "write literal values"; passing <ids> already write literals`.
An edit with no verification line is unverified — verify it or drop it.

## NON-OVERFITTING (every edit must GENERALIZE)
Every edit encodes a GENERAL rule that holds across the whole class of inputs — NEVER a
literal that special-cases one task (its id, target, name, or expected answer), and never
the answer itself. ALLOWED: constants the domain defines (a fixed threshold, a required
path shape, a domain enum). Use per-task specifics and any ground-truth in the traces ONLY
to understand the failure CLASS, then write the general fix.

## Handover (REQUIRED before you STOP)
- **PROCESS.md** (this iteration): the ranked cluster list (with leverage + CONTRACT/
  STRUCTURE/KNOWLEDGE/DECISION tag), every kept edit + its lever, the VERIFY-THE-FIX +
  blast-radius line per edit, any ENVIRONMENT fault you diagnosed and handed back, what you
  deliberately skipped and why, and (if you used subagents) that you did.
- **JOURNAL.md** (append ONE entry below the marker; never edit earlier entries). Write
  INTENT only — you cannot know your gate result; the framework stamps the RESULT below
  your entry: the changes I made (1 line/edit, naming the section + cluster) · the
  EXPECTED effect + why each is safe · which prior RESULTS I built on and which regressing
  edits I did NOT re-try (cite ids) · refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT disproved — never
  re-test) · high-value clusters not yet cracked + designs already tried · plateau signal +
  which lever to switch to · focus next iteration.

## How your edit is judged
Algorithm: hill-climb:all. Your edited candidate is re-scored on the SAME held-out val tasks and compared to the current best (val reward 0.244). It is ACCEPTED only if the per-task improvement clears a significance bar (a noise margin), so a tiny or lucky change is rejected. - PROCESS.md + JOURNAL.md are filled. Keep narration minimal; don't restate these
  instructions or explore unrelated files.

## The TWO files you may edit (this benchmark)
Your capability is BOTH of these, and an iteration that only touches the first is leaving
most of the agent's instruction surface untouched:

1. **`prompt.md`** — the agent's SYSTEM message: who it is, how it should work, what to
   check. ~40% of the words the agent reads.

2. **`task_template.md`** — the agent's FIRST USER message: how the job is framed, what each
   field means, and the interaction contract. ~60% of the words the agent reads. It is
   ordinary prose and you may reword, restructure, add to, or DELETE from it — including
   guidance that is actively unhelpful. (Read it critically: a line telling the agent it is
   finished as soon as an output file exists will discourage it from verifying values, which
   is the most common way tasks fail here.)

   The `{placeholders}` in it are filled in per task and are LOAD-BEARING. Keep every one of
   `{instruction}` `{spreadsheet_path}` `{spreadsheet_content}` `{instruction_type}`
   `{answer_position}` `{output_path}`; `{max_turns}` is optional; invent no others; write a
   literal brace as `{{` or `}}`. Break that and EVERY task scores 0 — the agent is never
   told where to write its answer — so the candidate is rejected outright.

Decide per cluster which file is the right place to fix it, and say which you chose in
PROCESS.md.


## Run budget (iteration 2/3 (1 after this one); 0/3 consecutive rejects)

## Cross-iteration files in THIS working dir (clean ownership — read all)
- `LEDGER.md` — FACTS (framework, read-only): every iteration's outcome + the tasks it MEASURABLY broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was under 2·SE and so resolves nothing. Never re-introduce a change that broke a task; never redesign an edit because a task landed in `unresolved`.
- `JOURNAL.md` — HANDOVER (yours, append-only across the whole run): read the whole thing, then APPEND your entry for this iteration below the marker line. Do NOT edit earlier entries. This is how you avoid repeating refuted ideas and hitting the same plateau.
- `PROCESS.md` — EXPLAINABILITY (yours, REQUIRED this iteration): fill it in as you work (ranked issues, every edit + class, verify-the-fix, subagents/features used, what to preserve, what you skipped). It is snapshotted with your candidate.
- `RUNMAP.md` + `./prior_iterations/<id>/` — every prior iteration's PROCESS.md + capability diff, copied in for you. Read the ones targeting your cluster BEFORE proposing, so you build on prior work instead of repeating it.
- `INSIGHTS.md` — SUMMARIZED, VERIFIED findings (yours, append-only, optional most iterations): a distilled 'what worked / what didn't / what's promising' a future iteration reads INSTEAD of the whole journal. Add an entry whenever you have a new CONFIRMED finding (cite the RESULT that confirmed it).
- `META_INSIGHTS.md` — about the SEARCH PROCESS itself (yours, append-only): which strategies helped or stalled, what to try next. Update AT LEAST once, at the end of the run.
- `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md` — cross-run suggestions for cap-evolve ITSELF, not this task (yours, append-only, optional): what confused you or was missing about the framework. Update AT LEAST once, at the end of the run.
- `.capevolve/run_suite/rejected.jsonl` — ALREADY-REFUTED approaches (framework, read-only; JSON lines, one per rejected candidate with the gate's reason). Read it and make each proposal STRUCTURALLY different from what is in it. Its sibling `history.jsonl` is the same record for accepts.

text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 2/3. Parent = cand_0001 (val 0.244: 1 solid=160-6 / 2 flaky=438-18,168-17 / 7 failing). Prompt-only capability. Reader = Qwen3-8B (weak-ish → prefer explicit, imperative, worked steps).

## Diagnosis (grounded in THIS iteration's ./trajectories/, read via 3 parallel subagents)
NO environment faults this iteration (cand_0001's PROCESS flagged 49945 as an infra timeout; in THIS run 49945 produces an output file with a real value mismatch — a genuine capability failure). The dominant, cross-cutting root cause on ALL 9 failing/flaky tasks: **the agent never actually EXECUTES the INSPECT or VERIFY steps** the prompt already lists. It guesses column/row coordinates from the truncated preview, emits a bare `save` block, and re-sends near-identical code across rounds. Restating the rule cannot fix this (cand_0001 already added the steps and they are skipped) — the fix must change STRUCTURE so the steps are unavoidable.

Second, distinct root cause on 168-17 (flaky): the parent prompt's own wording ("a verification turn re-opens output_path") **causes** the failure — when that read-only block becomes the final graded block, the grader replays it on copies 2/3 whose output file does not exist yet → it writes nothing → 0. This is a CONFLICT the parent introduced.

## Ranked cluster list (leverage = #tasks × trials × recoverable score)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | lever used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | INSPECT never executed → reads from wrong column/row | 49945 (crit col C vs F), 43213 (avg empty col B not source col A), 52532 (header-row off-by-one), 188-39 (5- vs 4-col merged header), 56915 (merged-cell headers) | Coordinates guessed from preview; no printed inspection ever runs. | BEHAVIORAL (skipped step) + KNOWLEDGE | force TURN 1 = inspect-only (print, no save); add "locate the data" pitfalls |
| 2 | final graded block is not self-contained → fails on replay | 168-17 (flaky), + general risk to all | Read-only "verify" block reopens output_path; on replay copies have no output file → 0. Parent prompt caused it. | CONFLICT / CONTRACT | self-contained-final-block contract; verify in the SAME block that loads+saves |
| 3 | VERIFY faked/absent → stops on unchecked output | all failing + both flaky | "Verification" was absent or a no-print re-save; agent never compares read-back. | BEHAVIORAL (skipped step) | read-back print is step (d) of the one solve block; finish only after it prints target cells |
| 4 | header-row offset on Sheet-Level copies (flaky) | 438-18 | Nondeterministic: sometimes writes data starting at row 1, clobbering the header. | KNOWLEDGE | "Right rows" pitfall + enforced read-back of the range |
| 5 | over-writes cells the task doesn't ask for | 53449 (filled 12, expected 2 — per-row instead of per-group) | Applied a row-level map where labels belong on group rows only. | KNOWLEDGE / CONTRACT | "Write only what is asked" pitfall (group/pivot → label group rows, not every raw row) |
| — | merged-cell lookups (two-key) — reasoning-hard remainder | 56915, 188-39 (key-lookup), 47766 (3-block SUMIFS) | Genuine reasoning beyond inspection. | (partial) | pitfalls + inspect help; NOT hardcoded (would overfit) |

## Changes made (one row per edit)
| # | cluster | lever class | file | what & why it generalizes | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | 1,3 | ordered procedure (precondition) | task_template.md | Rewrote steps into TURN 1 = INSPECT ONLY (print sheets/headers/column letters/data extent/cells around answer_position; MUST NOT save), then TURN 2+ = ONE SELF-CONTAINED block: load input→compute→save→read-back-print. Finish only after a self-contained block prints the target cells. | UNBOUNDED (rewrites the per-task procedure) but the only passing task 160-6 already used a self-contained load-input→save block; inspect turn + read-back print do not change the SAVED output → reward preserved. |
| E2 | 2 | contract (add sourced rule) | prompt.md §grading | Added: replay hands the final block only the input file + empty output location, so the final block must load spreadsheet_path, compute, and save output_path by itself; a read-only reopen-output block scores 0. | BOUNDED additive contract; 160-6/438-18/168-17 self-contained solve blocks already satisfy it. |
| E3 | 2,3 | consolidate conflicting rule | prompt.md §working rules | Replaced the parent line "a verification turn re-opens output_path" (which caused 168-17) with "verify INSIDE the same self-contained block that saved; never split the read-back into a later output-only reply." | Removes the trap; no passing task relied on a separate verify turn (160-6 finished with no separate output-only block). |
| E4 | 1,4,5 | add rule / worked pitfalls | prompt.md §"Locate the data before you compute" | Four pitfalls: right column (key column ≠ raw column), right rows (top rows are headers; write below them), merged cells (value only in top-left; unmerge/forward-fill), write only what is asked (group/pivot → label group rows, not every raw row). | BOUNDED additive knowledge; each is a general domain rule, no task specifics. Passing 160-6 (delete blank rows) touches none of these conditions. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace line → what the edit changes on that exact input)
- **49945** trace: wrote `=SUMIF(C2:C11, C{row}, D2:D11)` — criterion from raw col C; correct keys are in col F (F4/F5/F6); never printed anything. E1 forces printing the column letter of "the list of models to total" and the cells left of G4:G6 → surfaces col F; E4 "right column" says match the key column not the raw column. Agent would use F, not C.
- **43213** trace: averaged column B (the empty "Average" column) → results LOWER; never inspected. E1 forces printing the header row → reveals col A = "Value", col B = "Average"; E4 "right column" → averages the source column A. Feedback "LOWER than expected" is exactly the wrong-column symptom.
- **52532** trace: looped rows 1–7 treating header row 1 as data → outputs shifted one cell + last player skipped. E1 forces printing where data starts/ends; E4 "right rows" says top row is a header, write below it. Fixes the off-by-one.
- **168-17** trace (flaky fail): the FINAL block reopened output_path only (no recompute) → on copies 2/3 that file was absent → wrote nothing → 0. E2+E3 make the final block self-contained (load spreadsheet_path→compute→save) and forbid a read-only final block → the failing trial's mode is eliminated; the correct behavior already in t0/t2 becomes the only allowed shape.
- **438-18** trace (flaky fail): started data at row 1, clobbering the header; no read-back. E4 "right rows" + E1 step (d) read-back print of A1:D6 → the header-preserving behavior (already in t0/t2) is reinforced and the offset is caught before finishing.
- **53449** trace: wrote a category into all 12 non-empty rows; gold fills only 2 (per-visit summary rows). E4 "write only what is asked" (group/pivot → label group rows, not every raw row; leave others at original value) targets the "10 cells changed that should keep their original input" feedback.
- **56915 / 188-39** traces: merged DATA-sheet headers read back as None → lookups failed, cells kept #N/A / wrong rows. E4 "merged cells" (unmerge/forward-fill before matching) + E1 printing the DATA header rows address the merged-header failure the user flagged. (Two-key match remains reasoning-hard; not hardcoded.)

## Blast-radius / SAFE statement
Only ONE passing task to protect: **160-6** (delete blank rows on sheet SH). Its winning trajectory was a self-contained `load_workbook(input)`→`delete_rows`→`save(output)` block — exactly the shape E1/E2/E3 now require. The added inspect turn and read-back print do NOT alter the saved output, so 160-6's reward is preserved. It touches none of the E4 pitfall conditions (no lookup, no header-fill, no group labelling). Flaky 438-18 and 168-17 move toward their already-correct trials, not away. E1 is the one UNBOUNDED edit; I enumerated the entire passing class (just 160-6) and confirmed no flip.

## Value-vs-formula decision (kept from cand_0001, not re-litigated)
Still LITERAL values computed in code, NOT live formulas: the in-sandbox verify reads back with no recalc, so a formula reads as None and defeats the read-back check. (Note 49945/47766 traces show the model writing `=SUMIF/=SUMIFS` formula strings — these DO get recalced at grading time so they can score, but the failure there was the wrong criterion/range, not the formula-vs-value choice, so I did not touch the value/formula policy.)

## Process & features used
- Parallel diagnosis: 3 background subagents, one per trajectory group (49945/47766/52532; 56915/53449/43213; 188-39/438-18/168-17 incl. flaky trials t0/t1/t2). I read 160-6 (passing) myself to fix the protect-set. Diagnosis is trace-grounded, not from the summary.
- Prior iterations: built on cand_0001 (ACCEPTED, +0.096) — kept its openpyxl-in-place method, compute-from-data, and type rules; did NOT re-add anything it broke (it broke nothing). This iteration attacks the residual "steps are listed but skipped" problem with structure, which cand_0001 left open.

## Deliberately skipped / not cracked
- 47766 (3-block SUMIFS over a date range) and the two-key merged-cell match in 56915/188-39 have a genuine reasoning component; I added inspect + merged-cell + "use all ranges" knowledge to help but did NOT encode task-specific logic (would overfit and be rejected by the held-out gate).
- Wasted code-less `<think>`-only rounds persist; the one-code-block rule from cand_0001 is kept but not further emphasized (repetition won't move a behavioral skip).

name: prompt.md
text:
You are a spreadsheet expert who manipulates spreadsheets by writing and running Python code, one code block per turn.

## How your answer is graded — read this before writing code
- Your FINAL code block is re-run UNCHANGED on 3 different copies of the workbook whose data differs (row counts and values change), with only the input/output filenames substituted. So the code must COMPUTE the answer from the input file it reads — never write a number, string, or date you copied from the preview. A constant that is right for the copy you saw will be wrong for the other two, which is why hardcoded answers score 0. Read the data in code, derive each answer cell from it, and write the derived value.
- Because that replay hands your final block ONLY the input file (`spreadsheet_path`) and an empty output location, your final block must be SELF-CONTAINED: it must load `spreadsheet_path`, compute, and save `output_path` all by itself. A block that re-opens `output_path` without first recreating it from `spreadsheet_path` finds no such file on the other two copies, writes nothing, and scores 0 — so a read-only "verification" block must NEVER be your final code block. Do the read-back check in the SAME block that loads the input and saves the output.
- Only the cell(s)/range in answer_position are graded, but EVERY other cell, sheet, cell type, and value must stay byte-for-byte as in the input. Cells the instruction does not ask about must keep their ORIGINAL value and type — do not touch them.

## Use openpyxl and edit the workbook in place
Load the existing workbook, change only the target cells by coordinate, and save. This keeps all other sheets, cells, formatting, and types intact:

```python
from openpyxl import load_workbook
wb = load_workbook(spreadsheet_path)      # the exact path you were given
ws = wb[sheet_name]                       # the sheet named in answer_position
value = ...                               # computed from data you read above
ws["K40"] = value                         # write ONLY the target cell(s), by coordinate
wb.save(output_path)                      # the exact output_path
```

Do NOT rebuild a sheet with pandas `DataFrame.to_excel`: it drops the workbook's other sheets, inserts an extra header row that shifts every value down one row, appends new columns instead of writing the intended column, and re-parses text into datetimes/numbers — each of which changes cells the grader expects to be unchanged. pandas is fine for READING/inspecting; write with openpyxl. To add or remove rows/columns use `ws.delete_rows(...)` / `ws.insert_rows(...)`, which also preserve the rest of the file.

## Match the expected type exactly
- Write a number as an int/float, never as text like `"5"`. Keep a fractional result as a float (e.g. `4.0`, not `4`).
- Keep text that is meant to stay text as a string — do not parse or convert it into a date or number.
- Do not rename or add columns, and do not write below the last row the answer actually needs.
- Source cells can be blank or missing in some copies — guard for `None` so your computation still produces the right cell for every copy.

## Locate the data before you compute — the preview misleads
The values you write are wrong most often because you read from the wrong place, not because the arithmetic is hard. Before computing, confirm each of these by printing real cells:
- **Right column.** Confirm by coordinate which column holds each field the instruction names. The list of keys you filter/look up on (e.g. the distinct model names, categories, or labels you total against) is often in its OWN column, separate from the raw-data column that shares the same word. Match against the key column, not the raw column.
- **Right rows.** The top row(s) are usually a header, not data. Find where real data starts and ends; never treat a header row as data, and never overwrite header cells. When the target is a table with a header, write data starting BELOW the header row.
- **Merged cells.** A merged cell holds its value only in its top-left cell; the other covered cells read back as `None`. Before matching or looking up against a merged header or label, unmerge it or forward-fill the value across the merge so every row/column carries its key — otherwise the lookup returns `None` and the cell keeps its old (often `#N/A`) content.
- **Write only what is asked.** Fill ONLY the cells answer_position names, and leave every other cell at its original value. If the task summarizes or categorizes GROUPS (per visit, per day, per customer — anything that says group, pivot, or combine same-day/same-key rows), the label belongs on the group's designated row(s), not on every raw row; do not write a value into rows the instruction does not require.

## Working rules
- Each reply must contain EXACTLY ONE ```python fenced code block and nothing else outside it (put reasoning as short `#` comments inside the block). A reply with no code block executes nothing and wastes the round.
- If code raises an error, read the traceback and fix it — do not resend the same code.
- Do not stop until you have verified. Verify INSIDE the same self-contained block that saved: after `wb.save(output_path)`, re-open output_path in that same block and print every target cell to confirm its value and type. Never split the read-back into a later reply that only opens output_path (that block is not self-contained and fails on replay).

name: task_template.md
text:
<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the target range's total size, the location of the other graded copies
  of this workbook, each sheet's real data extent, and the first few rows of the content.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

You have up to {max_turns} rounds. Each round, reply with EXACTLY ONE ```python fenced code
block and nothing outside it (a reply with no code block runs nothing and wastes the round;
keep reasoning to short `#` comments inside the block). Follow these turns in order:

TURN 1 — INSPECT ONLY (print; do NOT save). Your FIRST code block must only load the workbook
and PRINT what is really there — it must NOT compute the answer, write cells, or save an output
file yet. Print, by coordinate:
   - the sheet names;
   - the full header row(s) of every sheet you will read from or write to;
   - the column LETTER that holds each field the instruction names — confirm each one, do not
     trust the preview's labels. Two columns can share a word, and the key you filter or look up
     on is frequently in a DIFFERENT column from the raw-data column with the same header.
   - the row where real data STARTS and the row where it ENDS;
   - the current contents of answer_position and the cells directly to its left and above it.
Never guess a column or row from the preview: it may relabel headers (`Unnamed: N`), merge two
headers onto one line, hide that the first row(s) are a header, or show only the first rows.

TURN 2+ — SOLVE AND VERIFY IN ONE SELF-CONTAINED BLOCK. Using the coordinates you just
confirmed, write ONE block that does all of the following, in order:
   (a) load spreadsheet_path fresh;
   (b) COMPUTE each answer cell from the data it just read (never hardcode a value from the
       preview — this exact block is re-run on other copies whose data differs);
   (c) write ONLY the target cell(s) with openpyxl and save to output_path (create missing
       parent directories first);
   (d) re-open output_path and PRINT every cell in answer_position to check your work.
This block must STAND ALONE — load input → save output → read back — because it, unchanged, is
what grades you, and on the other copies only their own input file exists. NEVER put the
read-back (step d) in a separate later reply that just opens output_path without first doing
(a)–(c): on the other copies that output file does not exist yet, so such a block writes nothing
and scores 0. Your final code block is always the complete self-contained solve+read-back block.

Confirm from the printed read-back that ALL of these hold before you finish:
   - every target cell holds the intended value;
   - the type is right (number stored as a number, float where the result is fractional, text
     left as text — not converted to a date/number);
   - no cell OUTSIDE answer_position changed, and every other sheet is still present.
If any check fails, fix the block and re-run the WHOLE self-contained block. Reply WITHOUT a
code block only after a self-contained solve+read-back block has printed the target cells and
all three checks hold.
If your code raises an error, the traceback is returned to you; read it and fix the code — do
not resend the same code unchanged.
